text: Sometimes, I just feel like a grouchy old woman. That's pretty much how Bommarito made me feel. Do I just have too high of expectations or what? I went into the process with a very, very long list of SUV's to consider and I wanted to drive each of them. I knew I had about 3 weeks until I could get out of my current car and be able to proceed with buying something new. Bommarito had the Escape I wanted (with all the bells and whistles, naturally). Rough start, my sales guy took my license and insurance card so that I could test drive and forgot to give them back. I didn't notice until I tried to buy a beer that night. I figured my bad for not even noticing and arranged to pick it up the next day. When I arrived, the guy couldn't find them!?! Dude. I had to wait a good 5-10 minutes to find the envelope he'd stuck them in. I will say he was nice enough to take some great pictures of the car and send them to me so that I could solicit opinions on the color - since I wasn't sold on the gray. Then, when I was finally ready to talk money I emailed him to start negotiations. I wanted to come to an agreement on price via email before coming in to sign any papers. His response was "Oh, we don't do that. It's dealership policy that all offers have to be made in person". Uhhh.. no? I'm not going to come in and waste an entire day negotiating a price. I'll go somewhere else. I told him that and I left feedback on their webpage telling them they lost a sale over these "Dealership policies" I was immediately contacted by several people from the dealership to let me know that was NOT their policy. In the mean time my salesguy emails me back.. "I'm certain our store's location is the closest to your office, anyway, so why not gather whatever numbers from wherever and email them to me. That way I can get an exception to our policy and give you a sale price commitment via email." Exception, my @ss. At this point the only reason why they retained my business was a) they gave me a good price and b) I was too lazy to drive to the Illinois dealer who had the car I wanted and all the options I wanted in stock We came to an agreement on price.. and of course a $200 "Administrative Fee" was tacked on at the last minute. My salesperson couldn't (wouldn't?) explain what exactly I was getting for that fee, just that "everyone has to pay it". Lame! If you're going to charge me a fee, you'd better be prepared to explain it. Now I go to pick up the car and there's a rather prominent black smudge on the tan sunroof cover. My salesguy immediately brings some cleaner, which doesn't remove the mark and smells so bad that I'm a little light headed driving away (considering it was about 6 inches from my head). Also, they have a checklist of things they HAVE to go over with you, like pairing your phone to the Sync system. Hi, I have a masters degree in computer engineering. I want to figure it out on my own.. LET ME SIGN something saying "Pass" and send me on my way! *Then* as I'm trying to get out of there on a dark cold rainy night, the sales guy starts asking what I thought of their Facebook page.. in a very, very slimey way he tries indirectly suggesting that I should go and REMOVE my comment from their Facebook page, to cover up for what he tried to pull with me! Yeah, that's not uncomfortable at all for me. Here is almost 3 weeks later and I do very much like my new Escape. However, I'm still rocking some temp tags. I check with my sales guy and he tells me that he "must have sent my school proof to Ford and they haven't processed it".. can I send it again? All over a $500 rebate and they're holding up my registration?!?! Still haven't heard anything back, my temp tags expire in 2 weeks and now I get to experience the joy of the DMV at the end of the month - assuming I even GET the paperwork without having to follow up again. Ironically, the Ford survey reminded me that Bommarito advertised free oil changes for 2 years.. but nobody ever went over that with me. I have no idea how often they'll cover the oil changes or if I need proof that they should be free. Sweet. One of their major selling points and they don't go over it? Bottom line? I got the car I wanted, they had it in stock, and I spent less than I was prepared to pay. Was it more work than I wanted? Yes. Did I end up with a deal? Yes. Would I recommend it to someone who isn't .. umm.. as strong as a self advocate as me? No. I can totally see these guys steamrolling someone else who didn't just go through HELL with another car and was not going to put up with BS from anyone else! Oh, but I did get chocolate chip cookies in the mail a few weeks later as a thank you gift. Is this what that mysterious Admin fee covers?!

The net result of the model has been that the wines, however well priced, end up being a couple of dollars per bottle more than the competition "all in". This is a merchant that I truly wanted to support, but ,after going the the ordering process more than once and cancelling, when the $40 per case shipping chargers were added, I decided that it simply wasn't worth the trouple and price ordering from H&G. The "discount the wine and make it up in shipping costs" business model is one that I found insulting. If you buy a $50 bottle of wine by the case, $40 per case doesn't matter. If you're buying an ostensibly discounted $12 wine, and adding $3.50 per bottle in shipping costs, the bargain disappears. I cancelled my subscription to their offerings. In short, the company's good palate caused me to subscribe to their offerings. The hidden charges caused me to unsubscribe. I wish them luck. I'm truly disappointed.

text: People go to coffeehouses for many reasons, and I can see why someone who goes here for something other than the actual coffee would give the place 4 or 5 stars. There's free wifi and nice pastries, and it serves as a community hub in a fantastic neighborhood. Upon walking in, I wanted to love this place instantly, and thought that certainly I would. Then I tasted the coffee. I don't know too many things, but I do know what a good cup of coffee tastes like. I did not get it here -- not even close. Now, I wasn't watching the pot all morning, so I can't verify for a fact that the coffee had been sitting in there for a long time, but it sure tasted like it had been sitting, and sitting, and sitting. I gave it the old college try, tried to be a good sport about it all and just drink up, but in the end, I couldn't make it to the bottom. It just got worse with each taste and swallow. I asked the barista what type of beans were used. She told me they were fair trade. Great, I'm all for fair trade, definitely, but: what type of beans were used? She did not know. Let me tell you, someone who works at a coffeehouse and doesn't even think to know about the coffee beans being used is not going to be someone who cares whether the coffee has been sitting out too long! After I left, still scratching my head about it all, I went to the website to learn about their beans, where they get them from, where they are roasted, hell, anything. Once again, there's just talk about the beans being fair trade and coming through the local port, and serious bragging about how good it is. You can even order a pound of the stuff, all without knowing anything at all about the beans! There's no information whatsoever provided -- no varietals, no countries of origin, no nothing. Would a place serious about its coffee think that such details are too trivial to mention? I didn't try the espresso beverages, so this review might not be relevant for someone who prefers a latte to straight coffee. And again, there are many good things to like about the place itself. But surely the quality of coffee at a coffeehouse has to matter, right?

text: 01/22/11 I called ARS about my stopped kitchen sink and made an appointment with them for 12 noon that day. The receptionist said it would be and we scheduled a follow up appointment for Saturday, February 12 to fix the problem. The technician was to arrive from 12pm-5pm. 02/12/11 At 4:30 I called ARS to get an ETA for the technician and was told that he would not be arriving at all that day. I asked the receptionist when he would be able to come. She said "I am not sure, 'probably' not until next Friday or Saturday". I told her I was unhappy with this news, that I had standing water in my sink and thought waiting a week for the company to come and redo a 2 week old job was inordinately long. She was of no assistance. She could not even give me a guarantee for an appointment. 02/16/11 I called ARS to see if I could get a confirmed appointment for the 18th or 19th. This time I was connected with Matt, (the first of the receptionists to identify himself) who was extremely helpful, called one of his supervisors and got me a confirmed first appointment for the morning of the 18th. I finally felt like my request for service was being heard. 02/18/11 The technician arrived at my house at about 9am and once again was professional and friendly. He informed me that my plumbing was not up to code so he normally would not warranty it but that this visit would be free. He was having a tough time fixing the stopped drain and asked me if I would like one of his supervisors to come out and do an estimate to replace the kitchen drain pipe, because he felt that simply snaking the drain would not permanently fix the problem. I agreed and within 15 minutes his supervisor was at my house. He was professional as well. After about 30 minutes the supervisor told me he'd assessed the problem. ARS would need to replace the kitchen drain pipe and connect it to my laundry drain. He told me that he'd been on the phone with HIS supervisor and HIS supervisor priced the job at appx. $3300 but that he'd told his supervisor the job was smaller than usually so he'd give me a 20% discount. The final estimate for the job was $2700. I initially agreed to this estimate but then decided I wanted to get a second opinion. This is where it gets shady. Up until this point I'd only been minorly annoyed with the receptionists' lack of service and long wait time, but had been happy with the technicians. I called ARS to tell them that I wanted to hold off on the job until I got a second opinion and was put on the phone with the technician's supervisor's supervisor, I'll call him "TSS". After telling TSS I wanted to hold off the appointment until I got a second opinion, we had a conversation approximating the following: TSS: "I don't want to lose your business, so what do you think is a fair price" Me: "I don't know what a fair price is, that's why I feel I need a second opinion" TSS: "Well I know we aren't over priced, let me have a look at your work order . . . OK YEAH, OH, I could have sworn the technician's supervisor said that we would have to tear up concrete, oh, well, in that case . . . hold on . . . OK I am about to give you a REALLY GOOD deal, are you ready?" Me: "OK" TSS: "I will take the price down to $1900 plus tax, with a 20 year warranty. Now you have to understand, I am a different sort of plumber . . . etc. etc. Me: "OK I will take down that price and get back to you once I get a second opinion." I called another plumber who set up an appointment with me. I did not inform the second plumber about ARS's estimate. 02/22/11 The second plumbing company came out to do an estimate on fixing the kitchen sink drain AS WELL AS fixing a pesky leak I have in my garden irrigation system. Though I appreciate the work that the technician did at my house, and his professionalism, I do not think the company prices their jobs fairly. Had I not postponed the appointment, I would've been swindled. text: The redeeming features of this place include location, and proximity to drunk people who need food, relatively fast and cheap. The "Philly Cheese Steak" is probably their most famous item, and it's not so bad, especially considering it's so nearby. The sandwich comes fully dressed, and is stocked with grilled peppers and onions. The staff is consistently bizarre. Sometimes brazenly rude, sometimes removed from reality, sometimes pleasant as if on Soma from Huxley's "Brave New World." Most recent experience included the grill cook who admitted he had been on the job three days, had no experience cooking whatsoever, and that tonight was his first night "solo." After getting the sandwich, I waited about five minutes at the cash register while the lady behind the counter berated at high volume a customer on the phone for attempting to place a take-out order. After slamming down the phone and listening to her various life issues, I finally was allowed to shovel a ten dollar bill across the counter to pay for my sandwich. Hey, it is what it is. It had goat cheese, pine nuts, spinach and cranberries. I was thinking it had onion, but didn't. Glad I got the dressing on the side, didn't like it but I'm picky about my dressings. Should have asked for some vinegar and oil, but that's fine. The salmon was good, but was only about an inch wide for $4. The salad overall was nice. My buddy got a pizza and it looked ok. He said it was good, but I though the crust looked pretty soggy in the center, but then again, it had a dollop of guac in the middle of the pizza. Food and service was good overall, the pricing seems high for Fountain Sq., but isn't out of line for the quality of food. Based upon their target audience, the dining room is probably just about right in this location, but is a little small. It is better than a big room that isn't full and a waste I suppose. I ate there a couple years ago on the roof, and because they have elevator/run stuff up there, it is slower and it can get hot if the sun isn't down since there is (or was when I was there) no real shade. The delay to get the food up to you can be bad, I think I had some pork chops or sliced pork tenderloin or something and I remember it was dry - I attribute it to the trip up to the roof as much as being a little over done. So your mileage may vary on the rooftop experience. If you get hammered up there, you probably don't care. I like the dining room better personally.

text: After hearing and reading rave reviews about this place, Guillermo's was disappointing. My wife and i went for our anniversary dinner and were really excited to go. For starters, the garlic bread was dry and hard. Then the soup was tepid -- just warmer than lukewarm. It was a hardy Italian style soup (pasta fagioli, which I usually like a lot) and it would have been good had it been served hot. The salad course was ok but also nothing to rave about. Tomatoes were fresh and the dressing was a nice, homemade style vinagrette, but some of the lettuce was a little brownish and neither of us finished our salad. Our appetizer, fried calamari, was great. It had a nice light texture and was tasty and tender. For her main course my wife ordered a baked salmon dish stuffed with Italian cream cheese and she liked it a lot. The fish was fresh and really delicious! I ordered a shrimp and crabmeat dish served in a creamy blush sauce over fettucini and it was good but not much better than I'd expect at a diner. (The server/kitchen staff did not wipe the bottom of my bowl and it got sauce all over the tablecloth.) Portions were good and what i didn't finish of my pasta dish I had for lunch the next day and it was tasty. Toward the end of our meal my wife noted how the server didn't even light the candle on our table and that too, though a small point, was a little disappointing. Bottom line, we may try Guillermo's again but with so many dining choices available, not sure if we'll return soon.

text: Half and Half is a great spot for a special occasion brunch. I came here on my birthday and left feeling very full and very happy. We came on a Sunday and, unsurprisingly, we had to wait about half an hour for two seats at the bar. This is actually my biggest complaint about this place - not the wait, but the fact that there's really no waiting area. We kind of had to stand around awkwardly scooting around servers, other patrons, and shifting chairs. The one good thing was that we were able to get coffee while we waited, and my cappuchio was one of the best I've ever had (and it was very pretty!). We ended up sitting at the bar, which turned out to be great. I ordered a cocktail called the Bacon, Egg & Cheese. This is now second only to Taste's duck fat cocktail in the wierdness factor - it contains bourbon, mexcal, marscapone cheese, a whole egg, maple syrup and lemon juice. It was fun from its uniqueness and had a great rich flavor, but I found the lemon flavor a bit overpowering (my friend said it tasted more like lemon pound cake than bacon, egg and cheese). For my food I opted for the eggs benadict with chorizo and avocado. It was rich, spicy, and completely delicious. The avocado really put the whole thing over the top and helped tone down the spicy meatiness of the chorizo. My friend's biscuits and gravey was also excellent, and contained perhaps the best biscuit I've ever had in Saint Louis. This place is pricey, but not absurdly so. You get a good amount of food for what you get, and everything is very high quality.

text: What a disaster - the worst mani/pedi I have ever had and of course it was the day before my wedding. I made nail/toenail polish change appointments for myself, my future mother-in law, and my mom for the day before my wedding a month in advance. Several days before the appointments, I received a call from Salon Fx saying that they double booked some appointments and did I mind if my appointments were pushed back an hour later? Well, I did mind, but I tried to play it cool and agreed, but confirmed that the salon would still be able to provide us services to which the person on the phone said, oh yes of course. When we showed up, I was taken into the back room with a woman who immediately said to me, "The nail technician is gone all weekend - I'm a hairstylist filling in, but I haven't done nails since beauty school." Really?! I should have just left then, but we were already backed up in terms of timing for the weekend and with my wedding the next day, I didn't know if I could find a new place in time. The woman was very nice but she wasn't lying - she really wasn't skilled at doing nails. I think my nails looked better when I walked in then they did when I walked out. My mother and mother-in-law smartly chose just to have their fingernails painted (not their toes too, like me) and also walked out with amateur-looking nails. My nails chipped later that night and I was happy I had a very light polish on or it would have looked even worse in the wedding pictures the next day. To rub salt in the wound, they charged us twice! I put a credit card down when I made the appointments, but when we went to leave, they made us pay in cash and said that the credit card was just to hold the appointment. Of course, when we got home, we saw the charge on the credit card. The thing that bothers me most isn't that the girl didn't do a good job with the nails - she's a hairstylist and it isn't her fault - but rather that the salon KNEW that the technician wasn't going to be there that weekend and didn't tell me so that I could find someone else. If they would have explained the situation on the phone when they called me a few days before the appointment, I would have understood and had time to book another appointment. Instead, they didn't tell me the truth and left me no choice but to have a horrible looking manicure on my wedding day, which is just unfortunate. I would never go back to this salon because I don't agree with misleading your customers and delivering sub-par service.

text: I'm somewhat heartened to see that at least a few eaters have begun to see through the hyped up fog that surrounds the Taco Bus as an outstanding destination for authentic Mexican food. Just because they throw a bit of cilantro into your burrito, or whatever, does not a 5-star Mexican joint make. Having lived in southern California, never mind extensive forays all over Texas and Arizona, I can report that some of the food put out by the Taco Bus does, on certain occasions, taste at least a bit authentic. And, from what I understand, the ownership has its roots in Mexico or at least a place where they learned how to cook real Mexican food. But my issues with the newish Taco Bus here in St. Pete revolve around over-pricing, serious under-sizing of entrees, and my general aversion to anything that attracts hordes of half-drunk 20-somethings who proceed to rhapsodize without really having any clue as to what they are talking about. I find the food here just okay, but really priced too high for the amount of protein they put on the plastic plates. Were there an overload of food, I might forgive that it now costs close to $10 at least to get a decent meal here. But they are very stingy with the portions, and therefore, I have given up this place. I do like what they did with the decor here: all open air and rustic, and located on a far strip of Central Avenue that needed some energy to help bring it alive. You can eat inside some little rooms with air conditioning, or venture outside either under a roof or into the open courtyard. I am not a big fan, either, of the non-stop Mexican music soundtrack of over-energetic accordians and blaring trumpets, playing 24 hours a day. It gives me a headache. In short, you can fare far better for your buck with cheap, but authentic, Mexican food elsewhere. Here, you pay for the hype, the surroundings, the convenience of 24-hour operation, the pre-food truck novelty of eating food cooked in a bus, and the sense that you have "discovered" some hidden gem. Not really.
label: NEG

text: I travel for business a lot (as Yelp can attest to) and this is the worst place I've stayed service wise. If this location had not been so conveniently located close to the business location I was working at, there is no way I would have stayed here. We had several people staying at this hotel over several weeks and all we heard was complaints about the customer service and the overall treatment from the hotel staff/management. The only good thing about this hotel is the rooms are spacious and the hotel looks nice, and is clean. Here's the list of terrible things... First off the customer service, it took me throwing a fit to get someone to fix the several issues that were going on. My company had organized us having breakfast coupons and internet covered and when I arrived (and all of my coworkers) they tried to tell everyone that this was not true. The place wants to charge you $13/night for internet and $15/morning for their below average breakfast buffet. After a fit I was able to get breakfast coupons and I was assured the internet charges would be taken off. This pissed me off already, but they take it to a new level, they reset a super-secret room based internet password every day at noon. It's the most asinine ridiculous concept for "security" I've ever heard of, and an incredible inconvenience to customers. As I mentioned the staff is just rude, they act like doing ANYTHING for you is the worst thing that has ever happened and several times I had to listen to someone at the front desk complain about another guest at the hotel or a co-worker, or about their job in general, while I waited for them to help me. My husband also caught the cleaning ladies gossiping outside of our hotel room making comments about us having the "Do Not Disturb" sign up for several days, he stepped out to confront them and they were surprised, apologized a bunch and ran off to clean. Just irresponsible customer service. Their breakfast, as I mentioned, sucks. Overcooked tiny scraps of potato for hashbrowns, rehydrated powdered eggs that have congealed into a slab in their chafing dishes, slimy sausage links and limp bacon, and biscuits out of what I assume is a costco bag that are rather hard. There's also nothing to put on the biscuits, I made the mistake of asking if there was gravy one morning and got a bowl of grey watery ... something. It was nasty. I wouldn't be so critical if it was a complimentary breakfast, but they're trying to charge FIFTEEN DOLLARS. Ugh. Last, but not least, my husband and I were going to stay an extra night and had called to add it on to our reservation, I was assured it was added but discovered the day before that they had scheduled it with a day gap in between, and according to the front desk they were "sold out". I was somewhat worried after reading some reviews of the place, but I couldn't have been happier with the level of service we received, and the quality of drinks and food. There were about 18 girls in our party, and we were given 2 large tables in a somewhat separate room (there were other people in there, but it felt pretty private). We had a server for each table, and I was very impressed by their attentiveness and accuracy, given we had such a large (and somewhat rowdy) party. They even let us get individual checks, which made everything so easy. I'm so happy with the service, I can't say it enough. The drinks: I stuck with wine, but I had sips of other's drinks to try, and all of the cocktails I tried were outstanding. The Plantation had a mix of gin, grapefruit juice, and basil that I would order again and again and will try to recreate at home. The Italian Greyhound was also a gin and grapefruit juice concoction, that was very refreshing and easy-drinking. Next time I'll take the hubs to try out the great-sounding bourbon cocktails. The food: Half the people at my table ordered the veggie ravioli, which was stuffed with Boursin cheese and was smothered in a fresh tomato sauce with big slices of roasted tomatoes and vegetables. It far exceeded my and everyone's expectations. Most of the other people at my table got the chicken, which looked great and everyone seemed to enjoy. I know one other person ordered the steak, and said it was fantastic. I think Eclipse has stepped up it's game, and people giving it negative reviews should give it another chance, even if just for the drinks. I'm very happy that I planned the party here, and I'd love to come back next time I'm in town.

text: I've eaten at Snockey's many times before. The last time I was there was about two yrs ago. I got sick but assumed it was due to me stuffing my face during clammy hour. The service was awful and extremely slow, the beer was flat, the oysters were not chilled....served on a tray with 3 pieces of ice. I absolutely love oysters and have eaten them at many places and never before have I had them served at room temperature. The clams casino and littleneck clams were mediocre, the deviled clams were blah, just filled with stuffing and the crab soup was nothing but watered down veggies probably diluted Campbell's. The decor doesn't bother me since good food can be served at the worst looking places. Finally, when we got the check (which was hand written by our waitress), there were many mistakes. Like I mentioned, we were there for clammy hour, which they advertise on their site and in the restaurant. The oysters were .83 vs. the advertised .75, the pick n peel shrimp was charged .50 vs the advertised .40, the flat beer was charged 3.25 vs the 1.99, the clams were .60 vs .50. We politely made mention to her that a few of the prices were wrong. She said that the prices were changed but did adjust a few since the prices were on the table. Yes, it's only a few bucks but it's the principal. I also understand inflation and the increase of cost but don't advertise one price and charge another. After correcting a few, the waitress' math was wrong, obviously she tried doing it in her head. Instead of wasting our time on asking her to adjust it again, we just paid the bill. I am not usually harsh especially since I love hole in the wall restaurants but seems to me this hole in the wall needs to be cemented up and closed down. The food is nothing special here. Yes, oysters are cheap, even at .83 cents a pop but spend an extra .17 cents and feel confident about what you're about to digest and hit up Oyster House on Sansom or McCormick's & Schmidt's for their happy hour.

The server mentioned it was gin, was that okay, which is a nice touch, she knew exactly what was in it, and that many people would probably expect vodka. I was going to have short ribs, until she explained the red snapper special to me, and I saw her serve another couple this plate of seaworthy deliciousness. I wasn't disappointed. A nice light white fish, with a beautiful crust and delightful sauce, served with grilled peppers and summer squash (could have done without the wild rice, not a fan of rice, but it was fine as the bed). My husband had the duck with a blackberry gastrique, it was cooked really well, and the sauce was a wonderful compliment. He loved the risotto cake that went along with it. The saucework on both dishes was perfection! We ended the meal by drinking our dessert. I had the raspberry lemon drop, which she assured me wasn't too sweet, and she was right on. Slightly sweet and tangy, just right. This is a lovely restaurant in Reno, and the fact that they source from local farms is always a plus in my eyes. We will come back.

As things stand, you pay $30 then are so assaulted by the jumble presented that the desire to escape wins out after about an hour. text: It was a chilly, windswept night in Philadelphia. We turned the corner onto Ranstead Street. I turned to her and said, "This is the part where you have to trust me." She looked back at me and said "I wouldn't have come this far if I didn't." A single door stood lit, alone in the middle of the block, beckoning to us, teasing what lies beyond. Traffic buzzing behind us, we stepped tentatively into the shadowy alley. A door bearing twin 'R's and a small window gave way to a nondescript foyer. The next door gave way to a cocktail lovers' fantasy. I can't really think of a better word to describe it than lush. Overstuffed leather banquettes, dark colors and candlelight, arched mirrors and curtains make it a beautiful anachronism, and escape to another time. Sitting at the richly appointed bar, our dapper server immediately appeared. After a conversation about our favorite drinks, he concocted two drinks based on our tastes. He gave me a Martinez, which I don't often get, and it fit the bill admirably. The rum based drink my companion received was a bit to subtle for her tastes unfortunately. As with many cocktail bars, your wallet suffers for the experience. I'd like to be able to follow up my first high end drink with something a bit more affordable. Ultimately, Ranstead Room really offers a great experience, it really transports you to an era of classic cocktails and class. It really stands apart from the Sex in the City martini bars of the 90s and early 2000s.

text: Last night my friend Rachelle texted to ask if we could meet up for dinner and we decided to take advantage of the city's variety by test driving a little Indian restaurant in Des Peres called Saffron. We selected Saffron primarily because of it's location [aka half-way in between the two of us], but we knew it was the right selection when we started reading reviews here on Yelp! Every single review raved about the delicious food and excellent service. Let's just say... even before ordering, we were excited. Now, I'll be honest, I love Indian food, but I'm not a "connoisseur" of it or anything. Most of the menu seemed rather foreign and so Rachelle and I ordered with our gut instinct and went with what sounded the best (and least threatening). This consisted of Chicken Pakora, Chicken Madras, and of course, some Naan-which is a traditional Indian bread. The naan and the chicken pakora arrived first, as they are part of the appetizer family. We choose the garlic cheese naan [because what isn't better stuffed with mozzarella cheese?] and it was delicious! It came with a creamy white yogurt sauce that added a nice, sweet moisture to the dish (which is naturally a little dry-as you would expect leavened bread to be). The chicken pakora was also very good-but not exactly what we expected. It was basically chunks of chicken marinated in chickpea batter and spices and then fried. I think that the friend appearance threw us off; but they turned out to be very good. The dish is served with three different sauces; one was a sweet and sour sauce, another was mint based, and another was tomatoes, garlic, and ketchup. Our favorite was definitely the delicious and tangy sweet and sour sauce-which is funny because our waiter claimed that the mint sauce was the "crowd favorite." [Apparently Rachelle and I are a little on the "odd" side when it comes to dipping sauces.] As for the ketchup sauce... it was surprisingly spicy, yet somehow that didn't overpower the taste of good old Heinz Ketchup; needless to say, we mostly stuck to the sweet and sour. Our main entree was the chicken madras, which we decided to order because the ingredients sounded so wonderful. This dish featured chicken cooked in curry leaves, coconut milk, ginger and fresh tomatoes-yum! This plate was definitely the star of the show. The meat was nice and tender, the long-grain rice was cooked perfectly, and the medium heat curry left us sweating a bit, but not gulping down water. It was sensational. All in all, the meal was fabulous, the restaurant was cute, the service was attentive but not overbearing, and the price was just right at about $15 a person. In fact, I would even be so bold to say that this was the most pleasant Indian food experience that I have had in St. Louis. SO, you should definitely check it out and let me know what you think! Happy eating!

text: When we decided to do a Sunday Brunch to celebrate three birthdays recently, we picked the Palace Cafe. Everyone else talked about their good memories of the restaurant. I went along as it had been a while since I was last there. We made a reservation for 11. We didn't arrive as a single group. Parking was mayhem on this Sunday morning, and the groups straggled in. The staff was kind enough to seat us at our table upstairs as we arrived, rather than make everyone wait downstairs until the last strays dragged in. Our reserved table on the second floor was ready, sort of. The silverware and menus were given out only when someone actually sat in a chair. On to the food... Of the appetizers, the crab-meat cheesecake a must order. The beignets were not good (I didn't like the one I sampled). Blue cheese salad was very good. When lunch came, everyone was served but me. Somehow my order was not put in. An awkward moment, everyone's food was in front of them, and my space was empty. Our server apologized for not having my food and said the kitchen was aware the problem and would soon have it out. While I was waiting, my husband finished his pulled pork eggs Benedict. I thought it had a good taste but it was cold. Not cool, cold. On my other side, was a cold crab quiche with spinach. When my chicken came out, it was like it had been warmed up with piping hot potatoes added to the plate. It tasted OK, but nothing I would order it again. When I had asked around, no one at the table claimed their food was hot. Warm and OK were the best responses. On to the desserts... We ordered most of them and passed the dishes around. The bread pudding, which is so raved about, I didn't think lived up to the claims. The strawberry cheesecake was good. The Bananas Foster was good. Praline ice cream was good. Service was poor, much less than you would expect at the Palace Cafe. I'm not sure the staff serving the table actually talked to each other. They were very erratic about taking drink orders. Ignore us for a while, then both would make rounds with minutes of each other, asking if we needed something. We waited a long time for food to arrive after we ordered it. My husband claimed an hour, but I think he was exaggerating slightly. When we were done, the server forgot to tell the kitchen staff to box our leftovers. Jazz trio played music, which was a nice added touch. Overall, too many good restaurants in the area to recommend this restaurant. The slow service and the cool food were major negatives. It's going to be a while before I consider returning to the Palace Cafe.
label: NEG

text: This is my favorite restaurant in New Orleans, and that's saying a lot because I've eaten at my fair share of NOLA spots. It's away from the touristy quarter on the quieter Esplanade. We stumbled in upon the recommendation of the innkeeper at HH Whitney House- a to-die-for bed and breakfast that is a couple of blocks up the road from Lola's. We were "done" with the touristy stuff for the evening and wanted a good, relaxed, close by meal. The sangria has spoiled me for life- most of the time I don't even bother with Sangria at restaurants or parties anymore because all the others simply pale in comparison to the bottled magic red Sangria they make and serve at Lola's. The bread is unbelievable and the garlic spread is to die for. The grilled calamari is very unique- a definite must order. The standout dish- and probably what most people visit for- is the paella, which is prepared FRESH with real rice- not the minute kind- so expect to wait about 30 minutes for your food. Completely worth it. It's amazing when you can go to a fabulous dinner and get two appetizers, two bottles of wine, three main dishes, bread, salads, and walk away for about $100. text: Interestingly enough, I received a message yesterday from the VP of Sales at the Chester Springs location requesting that I remove my Yelp review of the dealership because "a lot has changed" since I posted my comment, and because my comment is 2 years old. First of all, whether the incident(s) I described occurred yesterday or 2 years ago it doesn't change the fact that this was MY personal experience. I didn't realize there was an expiration date on my opinion. \sarcasm Secondly, my issues with the car were not limited to what I experienced and wrote about here on Yelp (so my bad for not following up) 2 years ago. I had problems sporadically up until the year my lease was up and I returned the vehicle. Since the engine was repaired for the valve spring (Summer 2009), the power-steering died on me (Fall 2009) while I was sitting on the Broad St exit of 95N heading to a Phillies game (mind you, I never attended the game because once I made it into the parking lot I had to call Roadside Assistance and wait for a tow), and finally the catalytic converter failed (Summer 2010) and needed repairs/replacement (I honestly can't remember if it just required a repair or if they replaced the part altogether - whatever, just add it to the list). In defense of the Service Dept, the service manager and I became rather close (super-nice guy and really went above and beyond the call of duty for me - replaced 2 tires, free of charge as an expression of goodwill). He made sure I always had a loaner vehicle at my disposal for as long as I needed. Granted this is something Lexus advertises as one of their many service perks, but many times I was showing up at the dealership on the spur of the moment and there isn't always a guarantee that a loaner car will be available on an impromptu basis. In fact, the time I took the car in for the catalytic converter all of the loaner vehicles were in use, so the service manager lent me his personal vehicle for the weekend. So my response to the request to remove my review? Sorry, but I stand by my review and will not take it down from Yelp. This is my personal experience and my opinion of the product. I gave kudos where they were due (and I believe my 2-star rating reflects that), however the positives and the passage of time do not negate the series of events. It is those events that led me to the decision to NOT go with Lexus for my next vehicle. Some people may swear by the brand and have experienced nothing but rainbows and unicorns with their vehicle; good for them - I wish them all the luck in the world. As far as my new car is concerned, I'm cautiously optimistic.

text: Sometimes an experience is so bad that simply contacting the owner is not enough. Tommy's original Pizza's staff is so incompetent and unprofessional that something on a larger scale must be done. The owner needs to re-evaluate how this restaurant is operated and investigate how their restaurant is run when they are not there. Chester County needs to do something to bring this establishment up to an acceptable level. The worst of their motley crew is an angry, rude and completely miserable waitress named Emily H. who has the attitude of a thug and has no business dealing with people, especially in a restaurant. After being seated by a zombie-like hostess we were greeted by a an angry, rude and completely miserable waitress named Emily H. who did not hide the fact that she was very unhappy about something and obviously did not want to be there. After receiving our drinks, Emily avoided our table like it was on fire. After waiting over 40 minutes for our food to arrive I finally walked across the restaurant to Emily since she would not come near our table, and told her I wanted a check for the iced tea's and the fries because we were tired of waiting and were leaving. Rudely and loudly in front of the other customers she said, "No, if you're leaving then tell them at the counter what you had." We received no explanation as to why there was a delay with our food, no apology for having to wait so long, no effort to resolve the situation, Emily just became ruder and more miserable than when she "greeted us" at our table forty minutes earlier. The people behind the counter found everything very amusing while Emily's anger became more vocal when she heard me explaining the situation to the man at the register. I said all I would have needed was an explanation why our dinner was taking so long. A few simple words would have smoothed the situation. Instead, Emily came charging into the kitchen and starts yelling at me that she didn't need to explain what was going on because I could see her standing in the kitchen earlier. Being a waitress, or at least hired to be one, she spends her time alternating between the tables and the kitchen and seeing her in either place told me nothing, I just knew that we were waiting an excessive amount of time for our food and that she was avoiding us. The crew behind the counter continued laughing and making comments under their breath, Emily continued her angry rant about how I was wrong to not accept the unexplained long wait. My wife and I should have just gotten up and left but I chose to do the honorable thing and pay for the drinks and fries. A good restaurant would have apologize for the bad experience and not let me pay for such a long wait but I had to stand there and be ridiculed by Emily and the staff while Zack took his time at the register. The final humiliation came while we were walking out through the restaurant towards the door when they started laughing and shouting across the restaurant in front of the other customers sarcastically, "Thank you, hope you enjoyed your dinner, and come again soon!" Under the previous owner Tommy's Original Pizza was a friendly, quality restaurant that my wife and I have been going to for years. Now it is a classless pizza shop that is run like a street corner. A copy of this complaint is going to the Chester County Chamber Of Commerce along with The National Restaurants Association. Businesses that operate so poorly cannot be allowed to continue operating this way and must be brought to a higher standard or forced to close.

text: I went to the Crescent Pie & Sausage Company because they have a sharp website, the food looked good in the pictures and there's nothing like some hot pizza to nurse a hang over. The physical place was nice. It had a rustically-modern-industrialized-warehouse feel to it. Peach painted walls, austere wooden tables, a hard cement floor and large, clean windows that allow the Mid-city neighborhood on Banks street to be a real part of the ambiance here. The music selection was blue grass and folk. I definitely heard a fiddle in the mix. I liked the music. I went there for lunch on a Monday. I walk in and pick up a menu from a pile at the front door. The paper menus are glue-sticked to pieces of cardboard. Swear to God...true story. Strange. How very...very...rustic. I curl my lip and the give a little pout- mainly because mine has a brown food stain on it. The cute waiter recommends the Chicken Marcella Pizza. He said 'it was his favorite.' I agree to that and an order of house made dill potato chips. The food was much better than dog food but not quite as good as cat food. The chips were boring, brown, greasy, overcooked and burnt. I guess I've been pampered by Zapps for too long. They looked nice with chunks of sea salt and fresh dill sprinkled on top but those fresh flavors couldn't breathe on burnt palette. The pizza dough was very thin and dry. It seemed to be having an identity crises. It couldn't quite decide whether it was a cracker, a tortilla or some pita bread. The pizza was dressed with onions, chicken, mushrooms, a Marsala wine sauce, Parmesan and house made ricotta. The pizza was bland, but the ricotta was luscious. It would make one hell of an addition to some manicotti (if the right chef was standing behind the noodle.) I left uninspired but I'm a big advocate of second chances. I'm not quite done with this place. Their Mac and cheese has gotten some good reviews and maybe their sausage is amazing. But, as of right now, I left feeling pretty disappointed and bored with everything I ordered...except the diet coke. The diet coke was exceptional.

text: For many years, I've heard the rumors about Botto's; mainly, that it's really good Italian food somewhere in the depths of Gloucester County. Whether it's from friends, co-workers, or even radio hits, I hadn't heard a bad thing. And this review isn't straying from there one iota. While awaiting my lass, who somehow managed to remember her phone charger, but nary a phone, I saddled up to the medium-sized bar in the lounge and enjoyed a tasty beer while watching hockey with the friendly, attentive bartender. Many folks were eating their dinner in there, but the lady and I were planning to dine in the full dining room. Once she arrived, we were whisked to a table just inside the quaint room. Twinkle lights and funky framed photos (many of Sinatra and the likes) adorned the walls and ceilings, and there is even a second-level balcony with tables. The food, however, is the star. It's a great menu. Plenty of options, from chicken to veal to seafood to homestyle pasta favorites. The complimentary bread was solid. It came with olive oil and fresh parm cheese that went together well. I ordered the Chicken and Asparagus with Penne, while ma'lady chose the Chicken Roberto. Both were gigantic portions. Mine included well-cooked chicken (strips, cut), delish asparagus, sundried tomatoes and a sublime white cream sauce. No, like, for real, that sauce was to-die-for. Hers included a generous amount of chicken medallions covered in melted fresh mozz (I'm a sucker for fresh mozz) with spinach and sundried tomatoes. It came with a side of fresh veggies and homemade garlic mashed potatoes. While tasty, it didn't have an element that jumped out like the sauce in mine. Very good meal, and the potatoes were quite nice. We shared the Limoncello cake for dessert. It was delicious cake, but the lemon flavor was lacking a bit. That may, however, have been the idea. The entire tray of desserts looked great. Our service was very adequate, even above average. The waitress was attentive but not overbearing, and never did we feel rushed despite being one of the last two tables in the joint. Botto's would be a definite recommend. While we had a Living Social deal, the menu prices are reasonable enough considering the portion sizes, and the quality is there, for sure. It's not just rumors; it's very good.

After being seated and looking at the menu we noticed that the only things on the menu were pizza and salad. The salads were priced from $6 - $8 which is pretty high for a side salad at a pizza joint. The sodas were priced at $2.50 a pop which always hits me the wrong way and the pizzas are from $12 - $20 bucks with toppings at $2 - $4 a pop. Geez, must be really good stuff! Well, our salad arrived after waiting about 20 minutes and it was suprisingly bad. Yup, the dressing was super watered down, hardly any cheese and I think they forgot the croutons. We sent it back and waited another 15 minutes for our pizza and some refills on our $2.50 pops. Once the pizza arrived I tried a slice of white pizza. I love thin crunchy pizza, this was thin and super chewy, stingy on the cheese and light on the garlic. I have had better every where I have ever tried white pizza. The other side of the pizza had red sauce with pep and ham. The pepperoni was the kind you buy at the store and tasted more like spicy salami, the sauce was so watered down that my pizza that was supposed to be thin and crispy was a soggy mess. Overall, this place sucks and I left wishing I ordered a $5 pizza from hungry howies. Thanks to the lovely waiter for refilling my kids juice with pepsi. I realized after they drank half of it. Warning!! DO NOT GO THERE!

text: Stopped by for a late sandwich for supper, and got there after they had closed the kitchen and the cook was leaving. Christina, who was still manning the counter, was most kind and quickly offered up Bayshore Breeze's Cuban sandwich as a good alternative. After eating this great Cuban, I think the Food Gods worked out my good fortune. Bayshore Breeze Market & Grill is located inside a very nice gas station/market right on the corner of corner of Alt. 19 and Curlew/Causeway Blvd. This intersection is directly at the entrance to the causeway to Honeymoon/Caladesi Island State Parks, and couldn't be more convenient to grab your food/drinks for a nice day at the beach. There are about a half dozen tables available for dining-in, and the entire area is very clean and neat. While they have a nice supply of prepared Cubans for serving customers quickly, I ordered mine with a twist, and Christina gladly obliged my custom order in spite of the late hour. You can't ask for better service than that. Bayshore Breeze's Cubans are not for the faint of heart. This is no wimpy sandwich. Just picking it up lets you know this thing is absolutely packed with meat, which by the way is filled with hand-pulled roast pork that the owner marinates for 24 hours in mojo, then is slow-roasted for another 7-8 hours before serving. None of that generic/store-bought sliced pork here at all, and the result elevates this Cuban far above most of it's competitors. Add in thinly-sliced ham and cheese, then tasty cuban bread hot-pressed to a perfect crust, and you've got Cuban heaven. And if you need any more to convince to check Bayshore Breeze out, go to their website and you'll find a list of online specials. They have multiple coupons which you can print out and present for breakfast/lunch/dinner/chicken pita/side order/frozen yogurt, and get one at half-price for every one you order. Even better, the daily specials page (accessible from the coupon page) lists a variety of different weekday "buy one, get one free" sandwich specials available from 3pm to closing. I'm definitely headed back to try out some other menu items. My scores on the "How good can food at a convenience store be?" scale: Atmosphere: 4 Food: 5 Service: 5 Value: 5

text: Stopped in for breakfast yesterday based on a positive but seemingly wary review in the city paper, and I think 'meh' is about all I can say. This place is way too new to have dirty silverware sitting on sticky tables; there's no excuse for that, diner or not. The ambiance is almost purposefully 'blah'. As lone customers, and with a total lack of music or any other background noise, we got to hear the small talk in the back among the staff while we waited a really long time for a couple of simple breakfasts. The staff is friendly (almost in an obligatory sense), and our coffees were kept full. The menu is small and unremarkable, the food is standard. My over easy eggs were good, my husband's french toast was a little bit soggy, the hash browns were just that - nothing to write home about, though not necessarily bad. Cheap but edible breakfasts are easy to find. This place needs to come up with some way to distinguish itself in such a vital neighborhood. Kitschy decor has been done, and total silence in the dining room is probably not it either.

text: There's a reason why the substantial parking lot of this run-down diner car is always filled with taxis. I know Pakistanis from New Jersey who gladly pay the $4 bridge toll to eat at this restaurant. I've tried just about everything here, and pretty much everything is solid. Some things are better than others, and some things (like salmon or chicken breast) can be a little dry at times. However, everything is really flavorful, and all the platters (~$11) come with rice, a huge slab of naan, a small serving of meh salad-from-a-bag and a veggie side. Each platter is a meal and a half for me. I'm partial to the lamb (both chops and kebab), the tandoori chicken is great, and their post-Ramadan whole fried chicken deal is pretty good. The spicy green sauce that comes with every platter is clutch, so ask for extra. For hearty homestyle Pakistani food-from-the-grill, Kabobeesh is the way to go.

text: I didn't expect to review a Red Wing shoe store. I frankly didn't expect to have a bad experience, I knew what size I was, what I wanted and basically wanted to be in an out without too much fuss. I realize the store operates 98% of it's time providing shoes for people who need specialty heavy-duty boots. I was in the 2% of people who go in there for a pair of good boots that will last me a long time - but don't necessarily "need" them. I am still of the opinion that Red Wing makes a quality product, but unfortunately I don't foresee me setting foot in one of their stores ever again. I'll stick to the basics and if for some odd reason the gentleman working in the store reads this - to help him clarify what happened that night. I walk in at about 7PM on October 23rd, 2012 - I don't know the name of the person working there - since I was never greeted, but it's not the end of the world. He's with two other clients and I can tell the guy is busy. I walk around trying to kill time and to give him time to get wrapped up - I'm in no hurry. I understand it's not the most ideal scenario and I don't expect them to drop everything they're doing - although, I can't think how "Hi, I'll be with you in a minute." would have cost him any time, but that's besides the point. A bunch of unacknowledged nothing happens after that I could be going around the store setting small fires and I doubt anything would be said to me. He completes the transaction with the first client, and I can tell he now needs to help client number two. I say nothing, I just happen to be near him towards the back of the store by the sizing machine. Suddenly, he snaps at me and says "You're GOING TO have to give me a minute DUDE - I'm the only one here." Keep in mind, I said nothing at this point. I am giving him a minute, in fact - I gave him twenty. Great first acknowledgement. I'm not the big traditionalist when it comes to customer service, and I'm not blind - I know you're busy. But if your first words to me are in that tone, then you lost a sale. It really isn't a problem you see - you don't want my business, and I don't want to give it to you. It actually works out perfectly for the both of us. This isn't the only source of Red Wing boots, and although I was set on the brand. Now I think I'm willing to give my other options a shot - and I mean that, I know it doesn't matter to this particular dealer, and I'm fine with that. . Of course, the boots I was looking for - Model 8146, are available at Brooks Brothers and I can tell you, the service there would be eons apart from this store. If so inclined, I may just drop by - but I really think there are too many options now that this sent me right back to the internet to look at what other alternatives there are out there. I appreciate someone is out there making an American made product, in American small business like these franchised Red Wing stores (dealerships) - I want to support that. But unfortunately, it's not worth the hassle of being treated like a nuisance.
label: NEG

text: In the movie, Away We Go, there is a scene where John Krasinski's character is outside on the beautiful JW Marriott Starr Pass Resort patio overlooking the desert while on the phone and trips over a wall. Little did I know that it would be the future "romantic" location for celebrating Bryan and my 5th anniversary. We booked last minute, the Thursday night prior to staying there and got a great deal for $209/night that included $100 resort credit a day. I even called the next day and said we'd be checking in late, and the front desk, replied, "Oh yes, not a problem, we will be here for you. Just get here when you can and safely." Aw, how nice! When booking our room, I typed in the small 45 character reserved comment space: "It's our 5th Anniversary!" so when we arrived the front desk greeted us "Happy Anniversary!" Since the hotel was so booked, they couldn't upgrade us to a suite, but they still had our signature view room with a patio balcony ready for us and they also gave us Elite access cards to allow us entrance to the Spa pool and complimentary valet and internet our entire stay! Go figure the first night we are there, there was a major water main break, and the entire resort was waterless since before we arrived at 7:40pm until the middle of the night - like 3am. We complained, so they comped us more resort credits for the inconvenience. We understood that it wasn't really their fault, but not being able to use the toilets, showers, or faucets was unsettling. The lazy river here was small compared to the one at JW Marriott Desert Ridge and shoved off to the side of the resort. It was disappointing compared to the lazy river at the Pointe where the sides of the river are covered with lush trees and vegetation, making it beautiful yet wonderfully shaded. Why do I still rate it high then? It's because of the service. Despite some of the short comings, they did everything to make things right. They were understanding and did their best to make our weekend special in spite of the chaos of it being Labor Day weekend. The resort was bursting at the seams with people, yet they had so much staff available to guide you to the right location or help you in any way that they could! The resort itself and its grounds are gorgeous! I loved the rooms too! They were still modern, but still had a warm southwestern flair.... Although we did have one little scorpion make its visit our last night, but luckily we saw it and killed it. (What do you expect? We're in the middle of the desert). Nevertheless, this resort accomplished what we wanted, which was to have a home away from home and a weekend of relaxation.

In addition to the standard Red Bridge, you'll find New Grist from Wisconsin, a couple other selections from as far away as Belgium, and hard ciders by Woodchuck (Vermont), Ace (Cali), and more. text: Ella's is where Bill and I choose to go for our friday night date night this week. What an awesome place! When we first arrived, it was very busy and parking was a little frustrating - however, we kept a postive attitude and didn't let it put a damper on our date because I REALLY wanted to like this place. We gave the host our name and what I thought was awesome is that they don't hand you any buzzer's or take your cell phone number for a reservation but, they remember exactly who you are. Very cool. We quickly made our way to the bar to have a few drinks before our table was ready. Let me tell you, one drink was plenty enough as Bill and I were definitely feeling a nice buzz before we even made it to our table! He had the Bloody Ella and I had the Cherry Limeade. At first glance the drinks are a little expensive but, they use high quality vodka and are WELL worth the price. We started with the "Viva La Chimi" appetizer and it was to die for! I absolutely adore mashed potatoes and this was pretty much fried mashed potatoes with a kick. As for our dinner, Bill had the fish tacos that are made with the catch of the day. In this case it was flounder. Bill really liked the tacos however, he is not a huge flounder fan but hey, not their fault! I had the good burger (veggie burger) and it was phenomenal! It came with sweet potato fries as well and they were not too sweet but actually had a little spice to them which I appreciate. We also shared dessert which was the King Killers. I HIGHLY recommend trying these. It is fried bananas and peanut better with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce. So good!!! All in all, we will definitely be returning to Ella's in the near future. Maybe to try the soul food sunday menu? :)

text: After hearing all the hype about the Hash House A GO GO in other cities and that one newly opened in Reno, we thought it would be a great place for a Mothers Day brunch with the girlfriend and her mother. I can simply say "THIS WAS THE WORST DINING I HAVE EVER EXPERIENCED". The wait to be seated was very reasonable, we were told 20-25 minutes and it was just that. After being seated that is when the disappointment started. There was an unreasonably long wait for our server to arrive and take are beverage orders, there were 5 of us, 3 adults, 1 teenager and 1 kid. After more time, we placed our food orders, 1 being from the kids menu, and so as we expected, we relaxed and waited for our food. It wasn't to long until the kid meal arrived but then nothing else, so after several minutes, the question was asked about the rest of the meals. We learned that the policy of the Hash House is, if you order from the kids menu, that is rushed out, so to not have the kids waiting. Unfortunately, the rest of the order is not started until all orders ahead are completed. The problem with this policy is that once your order is started, the easy items are completed and immediately sent out, the items that take longer, well they take longer. So looking at the time table, it was 18 minutes after the kids meal arrived that the next meal arrived, it was 29 minutes until the last meal arrived. Now to the food, the Chicken and Waffle breakfast was the hit of the table, the teenager was in heaven, it was HUGE and very good. However, the rest of the meals, really nothing special, I had one of the scrambles, the eggs OK, but the crispy potatoes, not so good. My girlfriend ordered the Blackberry Granola Flapjack, it was HUGE but also the worst thing I've tasted since survival school in the military and eating bugs. The granola was raw oats and the flapjack was undercooked, we all sampled it and the response was the same, NASTY. I understand this location is newly opened, 9 days now but this is not how you start a business and expect it to survive. As I read in other reviews, make sure you have a lot of time for a meal, from our arrival until we walked out completely disappointed, it was just under 2 hours. Oh, with respect to the kids meal policy, after hearing that from one of the manager, we watched other tables, it doesn't always work out that way. The one thing we did note was no table got all there meals at the same time, some closer but most several minutes between meals. It was obvious the frustration on the face of the servers, they spend more time apologizing to customers, than attending to them. That explains the wait at the beginning. I hope they can get it together, but it will be a long time before I waste my time there, too many options in Reno.

When it came out, all I saw was a patty lying in a pool of blood with melted cheese and a thick-ass bun on top. No, I didn't order a side of carbs to go with my soup; I ordered a burger. I told them to take it back and that I'd have a salad instead. The waitress looked at me like I had 4 heads, but didn't ask why. I wasn't up to explaining and so I ate my salad in silence. With pretty steep prices for mediocre to iffy food, I really can't understand why this place is such a big hit. Maybe it's the drink specials or the atmosphere, but really... a restaurant should have good food! Not impressed and won't be going back any time soon unless I have to.

text: Ok.... I am from Los Angeles, CA. I'm not trying to sound condescending, but a lot of the restaurants here fall short compared to the restaurants in Los Angeles. Can you blame me? You can't be from Los Angeles, New York, or Las Vegas and expect the food from Tucson to match up. I miss my brazilian bbq, I miss my 24-hour joints, I miss my legit taco stands, I miss my ethnic foods. My goal in Tucson is to find the best restaurants that pleases me and remind me of home. So I have been really disappointed with the quality of the sushi in Tucson, until I came here. My boyfriend and I drove around and 'round looking for a sushi place and I told him this place had really good reviews. Upon arrival, we see a quaint sushi restaurant and park in the lot next to the establishment. The restaurant was full so we sat at the sushi bar. There was one sushi chef (owner) and server working. It took her 20 minutes to take our drink order, but me and my boyfriend are pretty understanding. We felt bad that she had to take on the whole restaurant by herself and she was about my mom's age so I was even more understanding. My boyfriend and I stayed entertained playing hangman with each other. About an hour passes and we're thinking about just leaving, but the sushi chef sees me look at my phone to check the time and he hands us cucumber salad and apologizes. My boyfriend and I feel guilt and stay haha. The wait was totally worth it! The sashimi and sushi were so cold (like it should be! the only place that serves the fish cold, not warm) and melt-in-your-mouth good. We got the sashimi sampler, amaebi, yellowtail, salmon, tuna, masago, albacore, white tuna toro, and I forgot... but they were so good. The white tuna toro was only $7. I remember having toro at Mr. An's for $14! Total rip! Mr. An can go suck it! The meal came with complimentary miso soup and ice cream for dessert. After our meal, the chef asked where I was from and we were talking about Los Angeles and he taught my boyfriend a couple of Korean phrases so that he can impress my mom when he meets her. He explained to us that he usually doesn't expect so much people and we understood about the long wait. All in all, it was really good and by far our favorite sushi place (my boyfriend and I) :D We are visiting tomorrow as a matter of fact.
label: POS

text: Went here for a late night meal. We all ordered breakfast items except my friend who ordered a bunch of appetizers that came out on spears of Rosemary. They were alright. Turns out he was the cook who quit, which resulted in us waiting a ridiculously long time for our food. We finally got fed up and started to leave when they said "wait we have your food! We'll box it up". What they should have done was comped our meal for making us wait so long, but no here is your $70 bill. The food itself was a joke. I could have went back there and made a better meal. Will not be back, and obviously neither will the chef.

text: The hunt for the best Cuban sandwich in Tampa Bay continues at Alessi's Bakery. Alessi's is a full blown bakery. It's huge! They have a specialty cakes section. If their cakes taste anything like their pastries, they must be yummy. This place is a nightmare for carbaholics. Or heaven. Depends on your point of view. The rows of baked goodies are amazing. They gave us a sample of something. Don't know what it was, only that is was sweet, seemed like bread, and it was delicious. Focus! Order the Cuban and step away from the register... We ordered the "special" Cuban. I didn't know you would be able to feed three people with one sandwich. Thankfully I had already decided to split one with a friend, otherwise I'd be hurting. The bread was amazing. I love it. You'd expect that from a bakery, but I am happy to confirm these guys know how to make great Cuban bread. The pork was thinly sliced but authentic. The problem was the sandwich was too thick and was cold inside. I don't like cold Cubans. Next time I need to have them press it longer. For $6 this was the best deal I've seen. Aside from being cold inside, this was a really good Cuban sandwich. Problem is there were sooooo many other goodies that I have to come back. The sign outside said 49 cent brownies, limit 6 per customer. I'm sad to say I can't comment on them as I didn't get any. But I did have a bite of their carrot cake, and it was outstanding. I'm a fan!

text: Buuuuuuuuuuttery! One of the places that didn't disappoint at the Reading Terminal. These cookies were beautifully buttery. text: This place could do better in a few areas: --The music is hit or miss; good dj = good times, bad dj = bringing the party to a screeching halt. But there are posts and weird built-in benches delineating the linoleum area where they want you to dance (aka spill your drinks). Be prepared to be boxed in and jostled more and more as additional drunk people show up. --SUPER SOFT POUR DRINKS! This is the main reason I only give two stars. I always leave thinking "How am I not more drunk? Is my tolerance going up because I've been drinking too much lately?" No, it's not, they just water THE BEJEEESUS out of mixed drinks--I honestly think they just don't add liquor sometimes. Get shots instead, you'll actually get some alcohol. Another star off for only offering Patron tequila (it won't make people think less of your bar if you stock mid-level booze too). Drinks also come in pretty small plastic cups, they should at least be full to the brim guys! text: After a LONG work trip out of town and an extensive yearning to visit this hungry cat, I figured this would be the perfect time to break up the massive intake of steak my boyfriend had just taken in from the midwest with delicious "fresh" seafood it is known for. The curiosity of dining at this cat has stemmed for some time between my extreme love of sea food and cats, I have been clearly obsessed with the concept ever since. We had planned on eating a large dinner here which we mutually agreed on seafood tier tower 1 to share, the halibut for myself, and the stuffed squid for him. I did not even get through half of the seafood tower 1 before gagging in my napkin. I almost threw up at the table. The shrimp was VERY old. After seeing the look on my face, my boyfriend inquired why, and immediately instructed the server. Which apologized and brought out two more shrimp to make up for it. Okay, great. I was happy and then took a swig of a raw oyster, and then felt the same uneasiness and slimy, oldness as the shrimp. I put my fork down and decided I was done. My boyfriend, still starving and still open to the fact, opened a second 'makeup shrimp' and it was worse than the first. We decided to cancel dinner plans with the latter and agreed to go slices of pizza later if we came to be starving would be 100 fold better than risking the chance of food poisoning. We graciously took the bill of an appetizer plus my 2 drinks that cost over $75.00, and left. Seeing the post of only 1 day ago AGREEING that the shrimp is old before we even had a chance to review what others had said, I would be extremely wary of the freshness of the sea food and would take it as a serious health precaution to avoid until this issue has been sorted out. Our poor server was great, the quality of the "ever amazing sounding" seafood tower not so much. We are both now laying in bed contemplating on where to get a couple slices of pizza taking bets on who will be in the bathroom first.

text: I had a very disappointing dinner at this location this past weeekend. The service was good but the food was sad. I love Carrabba's and I find that it is usually synonymous with good Italian food so my dinner was that much more disappointing. Our starter of calimari was good and came out fast. Next came the salads (one Italian and one House) which had obviously sat around for hours if not a day or two in the kitchen fridge; the vegetables had dry edges and the entire salad was slightly wilted. DInner came out shortly thereafter and it was nothing special. The marsala dish I always look forward too and order was slightly oily and just didn't seem fresh at all. Trying to salvage the meal I did what I never do, I ordered dessert. I ordered one of the mini desserts and was sorry to find that it too had sat around in a fridge or freezer for at least a few days based on the mousse being dry and almost flavorless from freezer burn. I will admit it was busy when we went to the restaurant but we had an early dinner before 6pm and since the restaurant opens at 4pm you would think nothing would be older than 2 or 3pm. I worried the entire rest of the evening that I was going to get sick or at least have a stomachache from earting so much old food. If you're not going to serve fresh food then don't serve any at all.

text: Oh, Burger Up, where should I begin? I've given you more than a few fair shakes - four to be exact and every time I walk away disappointed and angry. Let's start with my personal biases - I hate large table seating. When I go out to dinner and intend to sit at a table, I generally expect it to be a personal table, an intimate experience between my guests and I, not a picnic with strangers. But I get it, it's a small space, and communal seating is an easy way to maximize volume. Also I hate the napkins. As someone who has worked in the industry for many years, seeing bar rags on my table (regardless of their cleanliness and starchy feel), touching my cutlery and, ultimately my face, disgusts me. Moving on to the food. Three out of four times, I've gotten different variations of their burgers. Fool me once, fool me twice, fool me three times - I just feel stupid. For the past twenty years of my adult, burger eating life, I have been ordering burgers medium rare. This temperature, in my experience, is extremely attainable. Sure sometimes its on the rare or medium side but who cares - it's not a filet. Nope, not for BURGER Up, medium rare somehow always turns out well done. Now, maybe I'm being picky, but if you are bold enough to name your restaurant after your main menu item, you better figure out how to cook it properly. The last, and final time I went to B.U. I ordered the citrus salmon burger, which managed to be bland and fishy without any sign of citrus. I actually had to ask my server for a lemon wedge to cut through the terrible flavor. Luckily, my server was near by! Literally. He was sitting at the table next to me, hanging out with his off-shift coworkers. The only thing that could have made my experiences worse would have been food poisoning.

The food is outstanding, as was the service. Our every need was met with such friendliness that by the time we left, we felt as though we had known everyone for years. The portions were very generous and left us feeling full by the time we left. This is true for both lunch and dinner. The desserts were delicious. The perfect ending to a delicious dinner or lunch. Angelo came to our table to introduce himself and find out how everything was. Now that's old school, something that you don't see being done very often! I would like to also say that the waitresses were the best!! So friendly and always at the table, tending to your needs. My husband and myself and our two boys (in their 20's) have found our most favorite restaurant of all time. We came in as strangers and left as friends!!! Thank you Angelo and girls for an amazing meal and a wonderful dining experience, every time. (lunch or dinner). So if you're looking for a new place to try, i promise you will not be disappointed. The food, the service, the prices and the atmosphere can't be beat. We can't wait to come back!!!! See you real soon.

text: The Pancake Pantry is a Nashville institution. It took me almost four years to get there, but get there I did! My husband and I had breakfast here with some friends, who insisted we had to, and helped us out with our menu selections. My husband, ever the steak-and-eggs fan, opted for that along with some pancakes, and I went with the Tennessee country ham with, of course, a side of pancakes as well. We split a side of hash browns. We're not big breakfast people, but I've gotta say this is one of the better breakfast spots I've been to. It ranks as well as West Egg in Chicago, M. Henry in Chicago, or Ann Sather (also in Chicago). The ham was perfectly salty, my eggs weren't too runny (I ordered them over medium), and the has browns were nice and crispy. And the pancakes? text: I've been there twice, both after Triple D was there. The first time was good, I stopped in during a normal work day and picked up a to go order. I drove about 5 minutes away and the food was still hot and tasty. The onion rings were great, my burger was juicy, and my wife's hot dog was really good. I went today. I think that a lot of people had the day off and it was packed. Most of the folks in line had never been there before but had seen it on tv. It took 30 minutes to get my order. Instead of the traditional wait at the window for your number, they were telling us to have a seat and they would bring it out. At the same time, they were telling people to sit down and they would take orders from the table. We sat and waited. When we go the order the onion rings were luke warm, my wife's sandwich was cold and the cheese wasn't melted, and they forgot one of the drinks. The would come out to take orders and the first table that said they were ready had their order taken. Unfortunately they started in the same place each time so the table by us waited for quite a while to finally order food. The couple's small child was getting anxious and hungry and the food hadn't come by the time we left. The other table by us ordered food and a milkshake. Their food finally came out without the milkshake. They mentioned it to the guy who brought the food out and he said he would check. About 8 minutes later another person came around and asked how was everything and they once again stated they didn't get their milkshake. No milkshake by the time we left. I think this place has good food but can't keep up with the rush of people that have seen it on Triple D. They are going through growing pains trying to adjust to the bigger crowd. When I left, all the tables were full (about half had food) and there were 18 people in line to order. My advice, either wait a month or so to try it out when all the fuss dies down or drive by and look to see how many people are there. If it is during rush hour and you see 10 people in line, decide if you have the time to wait for half an hour to get your food. Also remember, its not the just people in line, they take orders from the phone so you don't know how many orders are ahead of you. Or if you don't want to wait or eat there, call in your order and take it home.

text: Visiting New Orleans for Jazz Fest my bestie and I were on a mission to enjoy as much as possible in this awesome foodie city and Cafe Amelie delivered.
