After perusing their specialty cocktail menu we were both drawn immediately to the "cool hand cuke" a delightful cucumber cocktail that assuaged our hangovers and the heat without breaking a sweat. halfway through our second cocktail by the fountain we were seated in the sunshine and our waitress immediately moved to get us an umbrella as our table was scalding to the touch. we felt instantly taken care of. in no rush to order entrees, we made our way through the cocktail list trying just about every one (except the tequila cocktail served neat, it was a little too early for all that). we werent disappointed by a single one, though the cool hand cuke remains my favorite. our waitress, danielle, was super friendly, always there when we needed her as if she possessed some sixth sense for her tables, and was knowledgeable about everything on the menu. we started with the shrimp and grits appetizer, which despite only having three shrimp, was out of this world. i want to bathe in that sauce. for entrees i almost went with the shrimp and sausage penne, but realizing it was basically exactly what made up the shrimp and grits, i went for a plain old BLT and andy got the highly recommended cochon du lait and we each took half. the BLT was tasty, but nothing special and i immediately wished i had been more adventurous with my ordering. but as it turned out, it was a perfect balance to the half of the cochon du lait that was so spicy and flavorful and exactly as succulent as danielle had described. though the bill was hefty after 8 or 9 cocktails each, it was worth every penny. that courtyard is just so goddamn delightful. i can't wait to go back and try everything else on the menu as well.

text: This is an awesome joint to get your car twisted into new condition again!! So, here is the story about how I got into this outfit: While my ex was away at a conference in Houston, the city trash truck bashed into the rear of her Toyota Corolla and scraped it down the rear as it drove by. Of course, I can't prove they did it but I heard a noise that would have fit the damage when they drove down the street that day. They also left a residue on her car that fit the color of the trash truck. In any case, I had no definitive proof so it looked like we were coming out of the pocket on this one. I called her insurance company and they told us to take the car to the Mossy GMC & Buick dealership and handle the repairs through the insurance rep that is resident in the auto body department. I brought the car in, the rep examined the car and showed me her estimate for damages. 1400+ dollars would be the final cost to repair the car and it would also be 6 weeks before they could actually begin work because they were behind schedule. They even went so far as to charge for pinstripes and decals. C'mon, those should be free! In any case, since the damage to her car tore the paint off down to the bare metal, I didn't want her car going for 6 weeks outside suffering exposure to the elements. The LAST thing you want is additional repairs for rust-related damage. After taking the car to various body shops in Uptown, which were downright sketchy, I might add, I remembered Vargas Body Shop on Magazine St. while sitting outside one day at Nacho Mama's, sipping on a raspberry margarita. So, I took the car in and spoke to Vargas and his son about the repair. Vargas took a short look at the damage and said they could do it for a flat $800. I asked him about additional charges, such as paint, pinstripes, decals, etc. Vargas said not to worry about it, that it would all be included in the cost. Ok, sounds good. How long will it take you to repair the car? Vargas said to bring it in that day (which was Friday) and the car would be ready to pick up on Monday of the following week. I almost didn't believe it but I could tell they were confident in their abilities. I picked the car up on Monday and it looked brand new! I was really amazed. I tried to find the areas where they fixed it and I couldn't even detect it had EVER been damaged. I was very impressed. I went inside the office with Vargas to give him a check for the repairs. While I was waiting there, Vargas got into a VERY verbal exchange with someone on the phone who, based on what I could hear, was trying to wiggle their way out of paying their bill. It was funny to me how this little man exploded on the phone in a fury and then hung up and proceeded to cash me out as if nothing had ever happened. Reminded me of my days in Brooklyn, where it was common place to see shysters trying to hustle business owners, only to have them explode, throw them out and then casually take the next customer. None of this stuff should bother a customer, though. When you initially come into Vargas' workplace, it might appear a bit chaotic with parts lying about, cars half painted in the back, etc. All I can say is that if you're like me, all I care about is the final product. They sure delivered what they promised me, in the form of a timely repair and a lower cost than any other body shop in proximity. It's also worth mentioning that this body shop works closely with ER Automotive, which is located just around the corner on Louisiana Ave. Both are very reliable for any of your vehicle needs!

text: Not a very good start, Intermix! I was so excited for this store to open on Walnut Street. I walked in the new Philadelphia location this week, eager to check out what I thought would be my new favorite store. Not so. The only person who greeted me during the 5 minutes I was in the store, was the gentleman standing guard at the front door. I was the only client in the store, and all the sales girls were busy either chit chatting or fixing racks of clothing. I moved on to the merchandise thinking "Ok, the service is bad, but if the merchandise rocks, I'll have to suck it up" (kind of like my Zara thing - see my Zara review). Maybe it was the way things were displayed, but in the Chicago location, everything is highlighted in a way that it grabs your attention, it looks wonderful and makes you want to spend all your money in two seconds. Here at this location, nothing really grabbed my attention, it all looked drab, and the collection seemed a collection I have seen at other stores like Knit Wit. I didn't recognize any of the brands I looked at (where is my Rachel Zoe? Where is my Elizabeth and James?!) Even the accessories let me down, and those are usually my favorite and easiest part of shopping. Overall I was not impressed. Philadelphia keeps trying to add cool, pricey boutiques, but maybe we just don't have the right buyers in this area, at least according to what I like. I'll have to keep doing all my Intermix shopping in Chicago, and for now I'll simply hope that things perk up at the Walnut Street location.

text: Over the years, I've been to about a dozen concerts here at Verizon. Each experience has been a little different, depending on the event and where my seats are located. Like most everyone else has said, it's pretty...interesting, depending on the show. Kelly Clarkson show? Pretty tame. Lots of teenyboppers and 20-somethings. Pointfest? I witnessed a lot of pot smoking and PDA. Brooks and Dunn? Lots of older people. Low-key. Also, why was I at a Brooks and Dunn show? Don't hate -- they're actually pretty awesome. VIP seating -- I had VIP seats for The Fray concert a few years back. This was actually pretty nice; you're an enclosed space, so you have lots of space to stretch out. There's also a waitress that comes around and takes drink and food orders, so you don't have to leave your seats. Nice. Pit seating -- I had pit seats for the Jill Scott show last night. Pricey, but definitely worth it if you want the best concert experience. These seats are closer than the VIP seats, but don't offer as much foot room. For the VIP and pit seating, you're underneath the awning, so you don't have to worry about the elements (rain or blazing sun) ruining your time. The venue as a whole is not terrible, but Verizon REALLY needs to work on the parking situation. If you don't leave early, you're going to be stuck in the parking lot for AT LEAST an hour. It's a nightmare. Concessions are expensive, but that's to be expected. The people working there were nice enough. I really hate this venue, but I love a good concert, so I'm sure I'll be back soon enough.

text: I've not been in here in quite a while but I believe that my experiences in this establishment should be catalogued, just in case (why does everything happen to me??) A few years ago, I switched up from a shop I used to get 'my hair did' to this place on a suggestion from a co-worker. I'm a man and I personally don't mind a girl OR a guy chopping at my locks, so long as they know what they are doing and have the proper tools (OMG, are those pruning shears?! Get back, you beast! :: brandishes said individual with a stick:: ) Anyway, the inside of the joint was clean enough, although the overwhelming scent of styling chemicals placed me in an almost comatose state. Maybe that's their trick; lure you in with a coupon and intoxicate you out with products so that you don't struggle much in the chair, as they continue to hack away. In any case, the hostess/receptionist/whatever at the front counter upon entry was kind enough. I had called ahead and made an appointment with one of their better styling gurus so I hung out in the waiting room until she was ready for me. This particular stylist (not mentioning names) took me to her torture chamber near the rear of the facility, while asking me questions about my hair, in an effort to size up how much pleasure she was going to get out of having her way with my skull. A few questions later, she's off, chopping this way and that. In the process, she was telling me over and over how much experience she had and that those around her simply didn't have the skills she had. As she's telling me this, I began to get this searing pain at the back of my neck. I later got the same pain in other areas and it wasn't until I got home that I realized the pain was due to cuts she gave me with the clippers. Good god, is it too much to ask someone with elite hair cutting skills to have a steady hand? I like Katherin Hepburn and all but I would never have let her have a go at my hair in her later years! I figured that maybe I just got a bad crop that time around so I gave it another shot. This time, I was seated with a young, spryly girl from Dallas (again, no names....trying to be respectful). She had this inappropriate looking top on that resembled fishnet material and her boobs were practically spilling out onto me (as I'm writing this, I'm now wondering how many men are going to promptly make an appointment). As she's working on my hair, she's going through all these radical motions with her body, literally placing her boobs in my face at all times. It couldn't have just been coincidence. She was cutting my hair from behind me and still managed to find a way to get them in my face. How is that possible?? Plastic Woman, maybe?? Who knows?? I tried to keep my composure, as if her boobs weren't literally resting on my cheek, and start a conversation. After a while, she backed off on using her breasts to anchor onto my body and reciprocated the chat. However, very early into the discussion, the conversation took a grisly spiral into the underworld. She began to speak about her private life; some guy that she was dating and that he hadn't told her that he contracted crabs. She asked me "who does that to someone they love? Wouldn't you say something??" I was horrified but then thinking to myself "why are you telling me about this or even asking?? Further, what does it say about you that you're dating a guy with crabs??" I steered the conversation away to something else but as she was washing my hair later in the process, she started telling me about how she was unlucky with her relationships with men, that they are always into kinky stuff. Did she think that because I was relatively close to her age, I could relate?? Good god, if she brings up anything about a brief experimentation with a ball-gag, I am running straight out of here! Looking back on the experience, I should have left VERY early on, before she had a chance to get deeper into explanation. I don't know why I stuck around. I guess I was tired of fighting trying to find a good barber? No, that's not a good enough reason to sit there, listening to an employee discuss sexual exploits and STD's. Never again. I've since begun getting my hair cut at Stardust Salon on Magazine St., which is a much, much better outfit and I'll be posting a review of them in the days to come. For those of you thinking about using this joint, my tale is just a warning. You may have great experiences. I did not. Actually, I was quite scared. -3 stars were docked for the horrible stories the stylist shared with me. 2 stars were awarded because they actually do cut hair there.

text: My husband and I stopped in this past weekend for a tour (on Saturday), as he had a day off from work and the weather was beautiful. We figured we'd stop in as the brewery is in Lambertville, and walk over the bridge into New Hope for the day. When we arrived it was around a quarter to 2pm, and just in time for their 2pm tour. When you walk into the front door of the brewery, you end up in their tasting room. A lot of people were there that day but we made our way to the bar and ordered the $1 4 beer sampler, which was a great deal. My favorite beer on tap that day was the seasonal "Hippo-Lantern" beer (a Pumpkin beer). The tour began a few minutes after 2pm and, is free, in case you were wondering though of course I'm sure donations/tips at the bar are appreciated. The location is small so the tour does not last long, but you do learn some interesting facts about beer if you are into that. My husband and I are very much into craft beer so we enjoyed the information. I was surprised to know that they are only a 10 person company, wow. The company is doing so well that they are outgrowing their current location. At the end of your tour you can go back to the tasting room and bring home a six pack if you'd like. They also sell t-shirts. All in all an interesting experience and again if you are a beer enthusiast it's definitely worth a trip. If it's a nice day, you can hop on over to New Hope and explore all the shops and restaurants they have to offer as well.

text: Went here last night for the 5 course, $33 tasting menu that I have been hearing to much about. You don't observe it from afar while enjoying your meal - you are pretty much in it. The menu was the following: Fluke - This was sort of a crudo, the fluke was thinly sliced with sesame oil and some kind of vinegar/soy sauce. Very tasty, but small. Some kind of fish I never heard of - This was two tiiny pieces of fish in a pea- mint puree. I thought it tasted like bacon. My friend thought it tasted like grass. Just ok. Mussels - Fried mussels - yes, out of the shell and deep fried but without breading, with curry sauce and cilantro. AMAZING. Tilefish - Small piece of fish with asparagus on sweet onion puree with egg yolk. Just ok. Didn't taste the egg yolk at all. Strawberry Cake w/rhubarb - More of a cookie, and it didn't taste very strawberry at all. The rhubarb was in a sorbet on top. Sorbet on a cookie? Strange. Another thing I must point out is that when you sit down, they give you fresh bread and chimichurri to dip it in. I wanted to drink the chimichurri - enough said. This is a good choice for a BYOB, since it's hard to find BYOB seafood restaurants and the price isn't that crazy for what you get. But, if i'm going to shell out $42 total, I would expect all five courses to blow me away. Service was very attentive and friendly!

Again, looking at the old menu in my hand which I still owned, I ordered a large Buffalo Chicken stromboli (13 bucks) and a Fried Calamari Salad. "No seafood salads anymore, we changed the menu." Okay, then I'll just get the Misto salad and add shrimp to it. According to this menu, that should only run me about $9. Also, a two liter of ginger ale. Probably about $3. The girl mumbles something like "45 minutes, $37.50." I'm so baffled by a 45 minute wait on a Sunday night that I don't even stop to think about the price she tells me, convincing myself that I heard her say $27.50, which makes sense when I total up the food, tax, and delivery charge in my head. I get my cash ready, thinking I'll give him about $33 with tip. When our order finally arrives, it's, no joke, $37.50. I ask to see the receipt and I'm stunned. The buffalo chicken stromboli is TWENTY DOLLARS, a whole $7 upcharge from the menu and the salad is $12. WTF? I was going to refuse to pay but don't kill the messenger, right? It's not the delivery driver's fault. I go upstairs and get more cash than regretfully hand him $43 dollars. For 2 mediocre dinners from a pizzeria. On a Sunday night. After eating a sloppily thrown together salad with slices of store bought provolone cheese and FOUR tiny pieces of shrimp, I look at the new menu the driver gave us. The buffalo chicken stromboli doesn't even exist and the addition of shrimp to my salad says $4, which means each tiny shrimp cost $1. Ridiculous. I wish the girl on the phone told me that the stromboli doesn't exist and that they were going to make up some ridiculous charge because they had to throw something together they didn't even have ingredients for. In their defense, it was the size of a whole pizza folded in half, but they should still inform their customers that "oh, by the way, that'll cost you a whole 7 dollars extra." Needless to say, I don't think I'll ever order from there again.

text: After all the hype I've read from the Bucks County Food Blog and praise from Guy on DD&D we figured that we had to try this gem in our back yard. Wow, what a total disappointment. We did get seated immediately on a Friday night in their intimately sized dining room. My wife ordered the "famous" snapper soup and special handmade crab raviolis. I had just the handmade cheese raviolis (the ones featured on DD&D). The soup was just boring. Too quickly since we had not finished the soup or salads (simple side salads that are included with the meal and are served on too small of a plate). I am not a fan of crab, so I didn't taste her food, but she loves crab....most of the raviolis are now in a take home box and will find their way into our garbage later today. My cheese raviolis looked promising, with a bright red, fresh tomato sauce and a sprinkling of fresh parsley. But once I tasted them? They were really just not impressive at all. The cheese filling had a distinct brininess to them and a very grainy texture. The pasta was too thin and also flavorless. We definitely will not be going back if their two signature dishes (raviolis and snapper soup) are that sub-par.

text: This is my update and one written on a more serious note than the last more fluff-filled review of admiring the decor and playing games on my phone: This place is terrible. When I lived in some of my less-than-legitimate quarters of Chinatown, I paid for a mailbox at this location because getting mail delivered to my apartment was non-existent. Maybe I would receive a magazine here and there, but I would never have trusted bills or packages being left. So genius me some five years ago decided to pay the $75/year for a PO Box thinking that this would be the solution to all of my problems. Over the last few years staffing has been cut to next to nothing, where there once was a package pickup/shipping center there is nothing but a metal gate drawn. More often than not the line would be 20 people deep and with only 2 window attendants, collecting a package was an hour long endeavor. Around the holidays you can forget it, trying to mail packages would get you nothing but huffs and puffs from the long line behind you and eye-rolls from the employees. After awhile I just felt uncomfortable buying anything other than stamps or sending something certified or with a return receipt...only the bare necessities. Was this really what I was paying for? My last apartment in Chinatown was a major upgrade from buildings I had been in previously. I actually had a doorman, I had package receipt service, I had my own mailbox...my days with USPS were over! NOT! I put a forward on my mail from the PO Box that I had to my new address and thought everything would be just great. My mail was delivered no problem, I had a great mailman, I occasionally left him little notes to let him know how much I appreciated his service. So now we fast forward a year... Sadly I moved out of Chinatown, and when move time came I started to dread the mail-move. I went online to put a forward on my mail from Chinatown to my new address and crossed my fingers that my mail would start to show up between the 7-10 days promised with the $1 charge to my credit card. Two weeks came and went....nothing. Another week and I was at my breaking point, mind you I do all of my banking and bill-pay online, but this was ridiculous. I needed my InStyle! I called Penn Annex as they were my previous mail facility and was put on hold twice, 10 minutes at a clip...finally I get a hold of a kind woman who apologizes and creates a new forward for my mail that she says she will "hand deliver to my old mailman". PERFECT! I loved him! .... here I am 2 months after having moved into my new apartment and still no mail. What is going on with them? I don't know. I don't particularly care either, I don't have any other options for mail delivery like I do if I decide I hate PECO. I guess if they're the only option their assumption is that they can do what they want on their own time since you're tied to them for an eternity in post-office hell. I really wish they would get their acts together and I really wish they would start delivering my mail, where did it all go??

text: Annuals - 5 stars Food selection - 3 stars PLANTS/ ANNUALS This place has the best selection of annuals at any nursery I have ever been to anywhere. What the workers did not know about plants they asked the owners. They helped me troubleshoot issues with animals munching my herbs. FOOD SELECTION This place touts itself for being so natural and organic and holistic but I found their meat selection crappy and the workers extremely undereducated about their products and giving misinformation about how the meat is raised. I also bought some arugula pesto that was pretty gross. I was not here for a farmer's market. I was here on a regular weekday and happy to find an entire freezer of meats. I asked one of the workers if any meats are organic and she said everything they sell is organic in the meat freezer. But when I looked at the packaging, I was suspicious. I asked another person who worked there and she had to call someone on the phone to ask them. They used terms like "all natural" and "hormone free". text: After hearing rave reviews from friends and other moms, my husband and I took our 2 year old son to the Pop Shop for lunch. We arrived around 2:30, in time for a late lunch and we hoped no wait. We were wrong...we ended up waiting about thirty minutes until we were seated at a small table near the kitchen. You would think a seat by the kitchen would yield more timely service, but we were wrong there too. Upon sitting down we promptly placed our order (waiting for a seat allowed ample menu review time). We ordered the irish nachos as an appetizer, pancakes with candy for my son, I got the grilled cheese on a pretzel (because who doesn't like grilled cheese and pretzels??), and my husband ordered the Santa Fe. As it turned out the nachos were not bad, but there was hardly enough cheese for all of the french fries. Only half of the fries had cheese to go with them. My grilled cheese pretzel was really just a pretzel stuffed with cheese...quite disappointing. Somehow I thought they would have done something special with it, but I probably should have guessed. My husband's sandwich was nothing to rave about either. He said it tasted like a hoagie and we have better hoagie shops at home. Our service was mediocre at best. The waiter was a nice enough guy, but he was rarely in the dining area to check-in or for us to request a soda refill or more napkins. The atmosphere was good for children, in that there were a lot of kids and it was noisy making it easy on parents. However, the wait with a two-year old is not something to look forward to. Overall, our experience at the Pop Shop made us decide that it is not worth the drive, wait (both for a seat and then for our food), or even the food itself. I appreciate that I could take my son there for a meal where he could be loud, but it honestly is just not worth it. I'd much rather go to our local diner where there is no wait, impeccable service, and delicious diner food. We won't be back.

text: The Pourhouse is a new & cool joint right on Whyte ave. that boasts a modern and sophisticated feel to a place that is, quite simply put, a pub. Not a simple pub, mind you, since the pourhouse serves a really wide variety of "biers" from various countries, including some local breweries (local = Edmonton). In that sense, I like that the pourhouse has successfully marked itself as a unique little joint, among other pubs that are a stone's throw away from it. It's really quite an urban pub, with a fine menu. They have some space for live music and I believe they plan to utilize it. Tonight, while I was reading and having my beer and sandwich, there were suddenly loud voodoo like sounds coming from the front of the restaurant. After a couple of sips of beer, I began to enjoy the elegantly synchronized African-style drums that two musicians were playing. Now, when it comes to food, they've steered clear of the British/Irish pub food items that are invariably always deep fried things. Just three or four entrées are on the menu, perhaps in an attempt to lure the 1st daters to stick around for a full meal. Also, the classic burger/sandwich menu along with a soup & salads menu, gives it a very fine balance. I had the chicken sandwich with soup and it was really quite good. The price is not that less ($15 for an entree/sandwich and $6.00 and above for beers), but it's not targeting the routine lets-get-drunk college goer. It certainly seems to class up the act of Whyte Ave. True to a pub feel, they've decided to go with two of flat screen TVs exhibiting sports channels. However, with bright lighting and good quality furniture, this place is a fusion-style pub house.

text: New Orleans is known for it's non-pretentious diners and dives just as much as it's known for it's fine dining, and, to be honest with you, I prefer the more casual places over those with "jacket required." Of all the casual restaurants in New Orleans, Mother's is at the top of my list. Sure, it's well-known and more of a cliché when it comes to diner-style dining in New Orleans. But, there's a reason that Mother's is on top-- the food is tasty! I always stop in Mother's every time I visit New Orleans, and, on this last trip, Vinny and I stopped in twice! Once for breakfast and once for a late night dinner. On the 1st visit, I had Mae's omelet, which is made with Black Forest Ham. At first, I was caught off guard by the because the omelet had a hint of sweetness, but then I realized that the ham was cooked with a brown sugar caramelized crust (think along the lines of Honey Baked Ham). It was quite good. That morning, Vinny ordered the Crawfish Étouffée omelet, which was a simple egg omelet smothered in the classic creole crawfish concoction. He let me try it, and I must say, it was quite tasty! Another stand-out of this visit were the biscuits, which we gobbled down smothered in Mother's berry preserves! On our 2nd visit, Vinny and I ordered a Roast Beef Po-Boy, Red Beans, and Rice, and Bread Pudding. The Red Beans and Rice were amazing, but the Po-Boy and Bread Pudding were bland to me. I wish we had ordered the Ham Po-Boy instead. I'm sure it would have been tasty with the Black Forest Ham! If you've never been to Mother's, expect to see a line out the door. However, don't be discouraged because the line moves quickly Once you're inside, you place your food order at a counter and then find a seat and wait for your food to be delivered.

text: It's been well over a year since I've been here and I keep forgetting to go back to this Italian, probably because when you think of good places to dine, you don't think of Horsham. It's probably one of the best, if not the best restaurant in Horsham Township, I know that's not saying much, but this was a very good choice, period. We went during happy hour and sat at the bar. High ceilings, open atmosphere, wine racks behind glass walls, and doors open to an outside furnished patio when weather permits. Happy hour specials were pretty damn good, starting with $3 beers, all kinds, nothing excluded. They had a Victory Headwaters pale ale on tap. For $5 or $6 this would be fantastic, for $3, oh my dog, what a beer. House wines were $5/glass. And the selection was pretty damn good. During dinner we had the Montepulciano. A medium body, dry fresh Tuscan red made from the Sangiovese grape among others, this too was excellent. Happy hour apps, for free, and I like free, were hot wings (blue cheese dressing for the wings on the service table too), tomato bruschetta, as well as mozzarell and roasted pepper on the toasted Italian bread slices. The wings were nice and hot, flavor and heat, and the bruschetta not too shabby. Well that took care of the apps for this evening, and we saved room for an entree. I had the angel hair pasta with lump crab meat in a San Marzano tomato sauce. Perfectly cooked pasta, chunky tomato sauce, lots of lump crab meat, actually still in large lumps and not frayed into duty crab. My friend had the Lagostini, perfectly grilled Mediterranean prawns with artichoke risotto and asparagus. The prawns were light, sweet, tender, excellent. Service is usually good at the bar, and tonight was no exception. I've been here about 8 to 10 times and each time I say to myself "myself, I have to remember to come back here more often".

Upstairs, they have a huge wall-o-beer that lets you swipe a card and dispense (by the ounce) the beer of your choice! Amazing! The service was attentive without being annoying, and part of what impressed me when we first arrived was that they use a system for checking you in that sends you a text message when your table is ready.
